apush-leq-0005.outline: Context: European search for Asian trade after the Reconquista; diverse Native societies before contact. Evidence: smallpox and 50-90 percent demographic collapse; maize and potatoes reaching Europe; horses transforming Plains life; Potosi silver and global trade. Analysis: uneven, Europe gained calories and wealth, the Americas lost people and autonomy; some Native societies adapted and kept traditions.
apush-leq-0005.thesis: The Columbian Exchange transformed life in the Americas far more profoundly than in Europe from 1492 to 1607: it devastated Native populations through disease and forced labor while giving Europe new foods that fed population growth, a transformation deep on both sides but profoundly unequal.

apush-leq-0006.outline: Context: diverse Native societies and European motives. Evidence: fall of Tenochtitlan 1519-1521, seizure of Atahualpa 1532, smallpox epidemics, encomienda and mit'a. Analysis: uneven, destruction of empires versus persistence and adaptation, syncretism and resistance.
apush-leq-0006.thesis: Spanish conquest changed Native American societies profoundly from 1492 to 1607, destroying the Mexica and Inca empires, imposing Christianity and forced labor, and killing up to 90 percent through disease, yet change was uneven, as Native peoples adapted, resisted, and preserved parts of their cultures.
